correctness.rationale: For every field and finite simple graph, central inclusion reduces the problem to commuting alpha-planes; RREF pivot columns must form independent vertex sets. Maximality makes them dominating. Each nonpivot column is either zero or a scalar along its unique neighboring pivot, with a triangular zero constraint. The only remaining bracket equations are the squarefree products attached to cross-owner edges, giving the exact Stanley–Reisner chart. Nonzero supports count as graph independent sets. The witness follows directly from the Gr(2,4) Plücker relation. A separate standard-library enumerator exhaustively checked 235 graph-field instances over F2,F3,F4,F5 (F5 witness), including a genuine GF4 arithmetic implementation; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Maximum-dimensional abelian ideals are a canonical structural invariant of solvable Lie algebras, motivated by the classical dimension and ideal-existence problem. The result determines their entire Schubert-cell geometry and exact finite-field count for every graph, not just isolated examples or a dimension bound. The P4 versus K3 disjoint union K1 witness has the same ordinary independence polynomial and Lie dimensions yet differs both geometrically (two projective lines versus a plane) and in counts (2q+1 versus q²+q+1), proving the new invariant supplies information absent from the previously studied graph independence polynomial. The stratification supplies a reproducible enumeration and access to Stanley–Reisner techniques for further geometry, without claiming a global-component classification.
